_meta.indication: EVENITY is indicated for the treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk for fracture, defined as a history of osteoporotic fracture, or multiple risk factors for fracture; or patients who have failed or are intolerant to other available osteoporosis therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of romosozumab 210 mg SC every month for 12 months followed by denosumab 60 mg every 6 months compared to placebo followed by denosumab
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: subject incidence of new vertebral fractures at month 12 and at month 24
pivotal_trials.result: New vertebral fracture at Month 12: ARR 1.3% (95% CI 0.8, 1.8), RRR 73% (53, 84), P<0.001; at Month 24: ARR 1.9% (1.3, 2.5), RRR 75% (60, 84), P<0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, alendronate-controlled study of romosozumab 210 mg SC monthly for 12 months followed by alendronate 70 mg weekly compared with alendronate 70 mg weekly alone
pivotal_trials.population: Women with postmenopausal osteoporosis with a history of fracture
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Subject incidence of clinical fracture and new vertebral fracture
pivotal_trials.result: New vertebral fracture at Month 24: ARR 4.0% (95% CI 2.5, 5.6), RRR 50% (34, 62), P<0.001

key_safety: The most common adverse reactions (>=5%) were arthralgia and headache. In Study 1, arthralgia occurred in 468 (13.1%) EVENITY vs 434 (12.1%) placebo; headache 235 (6.6%) vs 208 (5.8%). Serious cardiovascular risk (MACE) drives the boxed warning: in Study 2, myocardial infarction occurred in 16 women (0.8%) on EVENITY vs 5 (0.2%) on alendronate; stroke in 13 (0.6%) vs 7 (0.3%).
target_moa: Romosozumab is a sclerostin inhibitor; it inhibits the action of sclerostin (a regulator of bone metabolism that inhibits the Wnt signaling pathway), increasing bone formation and, to a lesser extent, decreasing bone resorption.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: POTENTIAL RISK OF MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION, STROKE AND CARDIOVASCULAR DEATH — EVENITY may increase the risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death; it should not be initiated in patients who have had a myocardial infarction or stroke within the preceding year.

rems.type: The Applicant did not propose a REMS; FDA concluded a REMS is not necessary to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of romosozumab.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee meeting was held January 16, 2019 to discuss the cardiovascular safety findings. On the voting question whether the overall benefit/risk profile supports approval, the committee voted A: 15, B: 3, C: 1.

summary.text: BLA 761062 was a standard (non-priority) review submitted as a BLA resubmission after FDA issued a Complete Response Letter on July 13, 2017 for the original BLA over cardiovascular safety concerns. The resubmission (received July 9, 2018) was reviewed with an Advisory Committee meeting held January 16, 2019 (voting 15 yes / 3 different indication / 1 no), and the drug was approved with a boxed warning for cardiovascular risk and a required post-marketing cardiovascular safety study (PMR 3595-1).

requirement.text: PMR 3595-1: To evaluate the feasibility of a required post-marketing study assessing the cardiovascular safety of Evenity, conduct a study using a sequential analysis design to assess utilization patterns and channeling bias among new users of Evenity compared to new users of other anti-osteoporosis therapies.
